This article analyzes the types of surgical procedures performed on patients with Inflammatory Bowel Disease (IBD), tracked under [[indikator-6|Indikator 6]]. The data covers the reporting period from October 1, 2023, to September 30, 2024, detailing the frequency of specific SMR procedure codes [^src1].

Laparoscopic procedures dominate the most frequently performed surgeries. The leader is KJFB21 (Laparoskopisk ileocøkal resektion), which was performed 114 times, accounting for 10.8% of the recorded operations [^src1]. This is closely followed by KJFH11 (Laparoskopisk kolektomi og ileostomi) with 106 procedures (10.1%) and KJAH01 (Laparoskopi) with 78 procedures (7.4%) [^src1]. 

At the lower end of the spectrum, several specialized or less common procedures were performed only 5 times each (0.5%), including KJGB32 (Abdominal og intersphincterisk excision af endetarm), KJAH33 (Åbning af laparostomi), KJFA60 (Tarmplastik ved striktur i tyndtarm), KJFC00 (Enteroenterostomi), KJFG40K (Åben operation for stomihernie med anvendelse af m), and KJFG41A (Laparoskopisk operation for stomihernie) [^src1]. 

A notable outlier in the dataset is the "Øvrige" (Other) category, which recorded the highest single count of 123 procedures, representing 11.7% of the total [^src1]. This indicates that a significant portion of surgical interventions for IBD patients fall outside the most common specific procedure codes listed. Because the available data consists of only a single reporting period, no longitudinal trends regarding the increase or decline of specific surgical methods can be established. Furthermore, the dataset does not define specific clinical targets or thresholds to evaluate whether met or missed.
